Have bread makers evolved over time? I had one YEARS ago and it was convenient. I bake now most weekends if I'm home

I don't think so, at least not in the last 7 years since I have had my machine. Basically I still see pretty much the same "top models" around.

I guess some minor improvements came around, say: more silent, a few more fancy options to deal with special stuff (whole wheat, etc.), but outside of that, I haven't seen anything new. (Was curious months ago and checked what was available)
Do you occasionally make your own bread? I also wonder if we can use our own recipes (more proportions) in these machines.

In my case it's about periods, sometimes I just get tired of bread and stop making it, others it's just faster to go buy it and sometimes the bread from the machine is not exactly ideal for whatever I want to make. So yeah, I do use the machine but not all the time.

And of course you can use your own recipes, my personal favorite is a milk bread with a delicate sweet flavor (from honey and cornstarch) and another I make frequently is an egg and oats bread when I want a more nutritious bread. The trick is in understanding the basics and experiment.

Usually these machines come with their own recipes, start from there, adjust to your needs and then do your own thing. I don't recommend doing your own recipes from the beginning since you are going to screw up frequently and a lot of perfectly good ingredients will be lost. As you can imagine, unlike making bread by hand, you really can't control and adjust in the middle of the process. Just pay attention to the recipes and you will understand the patterns of them, then improvise. For example (not an actual recipe): most recipes combine 15 oz of flour with 10 oz of liquid, then I can add 5 oz of whatever I want as long as it's not a liquid or I can change part of that liquid with another liquid as long as they total 10 oz, etc.

In any case, if you are curious, don't hesitate to ask anything you may want to know. In a curious case, we changed the yeast we were using for years from the one recommended by the manufacturer with another one and the results were arguably better. (Probably not an issue of the manufacturer but just that the other yeast was of better quality)
